Desc.AllPrograms: The 'All Programs' module of Tranal Uninstaller Pro shows every installed program, split into two default groups: 'New' and 'Other'. In the 'Details' view or through the context menu you can get extra information (links and properties) about these programs. This module's settings are located in the Options menu.
Desc.TracedPrograms: The 'Monitored Programs' module of Tranal Uninstaller Pro lets you trace program installations. Every program installed with tracing produces a log with the files, folders and registry keys it created, which allows a precise uninstall.
Desc.WindowsApps: The 'Windows Apps' module of Tranal Uninstaller Pro lets you uninstall Windows Store applications installed for the current user.
Desc.BrowserExtensions: The 'Browser Extensions' module of Tranal Uninstaller Pro lets you remove extensions installed in the Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Opera browsers, including from the user profiles.
Desc.LogsDatabase: The 'Logs Database' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro keeps the logs of traced installations. Logs can be imported, exported and used to uninstall with precision.
Desc.HunterMode: The 'Hunter Mode' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro lets you uninstall programs from a desktop icon: drag the icon onto the Tranal window to uninstall the associated program.
Desc.AutorunManager: The 'Autorun Manager' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro manages the items that start automatically with Windows: Run registry keys, services, scheduled tasks and startup folders.
Desc.JunkCleaner: The 'Junk Files Cleaner' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro scans and removes temporary files, caches, logs and thumbnails that take up unnecessary disk space.
Desc.WindowsTools: The 'Windows Tools' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro give quick access to the native Windows utilities: disk cleanup, defragmentation, services, scheduled tasks, device manager and more.
Desc.HistoryCleaner: The 'History Cleaner' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro clears the run history, the clipboard, recent items and the search history.
Desc.EvidenceRemover: The 'Evidence Remover' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro removes traces of use: prefetch, Explorer history, jump lists, recent documents, event logs and the DNS cache.
Desc.UnrecoverableDelete: The 'Unrecoverable Delete' of Tranal Uninstaller Pro overwrites the content of the files before deleting them, so they cannot be recovered by data-recovery tools.

Guide.Central.What: Gathers in one place what needs attention on the computer: program leftovers, items that slow Windows down and recent failures.
Guide.Central.Gain: A quick health summary of the PC, with a shortcut to the tool that fixes each item.
Guide.Central.When: When you don't know where to start and want to see what is worth fixing.
Guide.Central.Avoid: It only points out problems; nothing is removed until you open the tool and confirm.
Guide.TracedPrograms.What: Shows the programs whose installation was traced by Tranal, with the exact list of files and registry keys each one created.
Guide.TracedPrograms.Gain: The cleanest uninstall possible: Tranal knows exactly what the program put on the PC.
Guide.TracedPrograms.When: To remove a program you installed with Tranal's install monitor turned on.
Guide.TracedPrograms.Avoid: If the list is empty, no installation was traced. Use the regular program list.
Guide.WindowsApps.What: Lists Microsoft Store apps and the apps that ship with Windows (Photos, Weather, Xbox…) installed for your account.
Guide.WindowsApps.Gain: Remove apps you never use that take up space or clutter the Start menu.
Guide.WindowsApps.When: When you want to remove a Store app or a preinstalled Windows app.
Guide.WindowsApps.Avoid: Avoid removing system apps you don't recognize (like the Store itself or the Photos viewer): other features may depend on them.
Guide.BrowserExtensions.What: Lists the extensions installed in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Opera, across all profiles.
Guide.BrowserExtensions.Gain: Find and remove forgotten, unknown or suspicious extensions that slow the browser down or change your home page.
Guide.BrowserExtensions.When: When the browser got slow, shows ads or changed its home page on its own.
Guide.BrowserExtensions.Avoid: Close the browser before removing. Don't remove extensions you rely on (a password manager, for example).
Guide.LogsDatabase.What: Stores the installation logs traced by Tranal: what each installation created on the system.
Guide.LogsDatabase.Gain: You can import, export and reuse these logs to uninstall precisely.
Guide.LogsDatabase.When: To check what an installer did or take a log to another computer.
Guide.LogsDatabase.Avoid: Without traced installations the database is empty — there is nothing to do here.
Guide.HunterMode.What: Lets you pick a program by pointing at its icon on the desktop or in the tray, without searching the list.
Guide.HunterMode.Gain: Quickly find which program is behind an icon or window.
Guide.HunterMode.When: When you see an icon and don't know which program it is or how to remove it.
Guide.HunterMode.Avoid: If you already know the program's name, searching the list is simpler.
Guide.AutorunManager.What: Lists everything that starts on its own with Windows: startup programs, services and scheduled tasks.
Guide.AutorunManager.Gain: A Windows that boots faster and runs lighter, by turning off what you don't need at startup.
Guide.AutorunManager.When: When the PC takes long to start or programs you didn't ask for are already open.
Guide.AutorunManager.Avoid: Don't disable antivirus, drivers (sound, video, touchpad) or manufacturer items you don't recognize. When in doubt, disable instead of deleting.
Guide.BootCenter.What: Shows how long Windows took to start and which items start with it, with the option to create or pause items.
Guide.BootCenter.Gain: Understand what weighs on startup and measure whether a change helped.
Guide.BootCenter.When: After installing many programs, to see what joined the startup.
Guide.BootCenter.Avoid: To simply turn off startup programs, the Autorun Manager is more direct.
Guide.ActiveFiles.What: Shows which programs are using a file right now.
Guide.ActiveFiles.Gain: Find out why Windows says a file is in use and won't let you delete or move it.
Guide.ActiveFiles.When: When a file can't be deleted, renamed or moved.
Guide.ActiveFiles.Avoid: It only works for files you pick; to release the file, use the Unlocker.
Guide.FileAssociator.What: Shows which program opens each file type (.pdf, .jpg, .mp4…).
Guide.FileAssociator.Gain: Fix files that open in the wrong program or lost their program after an uninstall.
Guide.FileAssociator.When: When a file type opens in the wrong program or asks you to choose an app.
Guide.FileAssociator.Avoid: Don't change associations of system types (.exe, .lnk, .bat): Windows may stop opening programs.
Guide.UndoCenter.What: Records what Tranal changed on the computer (uninstalls, cleanups, removals) and keeps the backup of each change.
Guide.UndoCenter.Gain: Undo a removal that went wrong and bring back what was deleted.
Guide.UndoCenter.When: When something stopped working after a cleanup or uninstall.
Guide.UndoCenter.Avoid: Only changes that had a backup can be undone: changes made outside Tranal don't appear here.
Guide.FileOwnership.What: Shows and fixes the owner of files and folders that Windows won't let you touch.
Guide.FileOwnership.Gain: Delete leftovers that give "access denied" even for the administrator.
Guide.FileOwnership.When: When a folder of an already uninstalled program can't be deleted for lack of permission.
Guide.FileOwnership.Avoid: Never change ownership of Windows folders (C:\Windows, the whole Program Files): it can break the system.
Guide.DeepAnalysis.What: Gathers everything Tranal knows about a program: registry, folders, services, startup, signature and more.
Guide.DeepAnalysis.Gain: A complete view of a program before deciding to remove it.
Guide.DeepAnalysis.When: To investigate an unknown or suspicious program.
Guide.DeepAnalysis.Avoid: It is not needed to uninstall: the regular uninstall already searches for leftovers.
Guide.InstallerGuard.What: Shows how Tranal recognizes that a file is an installer (signature, name, packager).
Guide.InstallerGuard.Gain: Know what Tranal monitors when you install something.
Guide.InstallerGuard.When: When you want to understand or adjust installer recognition.
Guide.InstallerGuard.Avoid: For everyday use there is no need to change anything here.
Guide.FailedUninstalls.What: Lists the uninstalls that failed, with the error code and message.
Guide.FailedUninstalls.Gain: Understand why a program didn't go away and retry the right way (for example, with forced uninstall).
Guide.FailedUninstalls.When: When a program is still in the list after being uninstalled.
Guide.FailedUninstalls.Avoid: If nothing failed, the list is empty.
Guide.PowerPlan.What: Schedules shutdown, restart, sleep or hibernate with a countdown.
Guide.PowerPlan.Gain: Let the PC finish a long task and turn off by itself.
Guide.PowerPlan.When: Before a long uninstall or cleanup, when you're stepping away.
Guide.PowerPlan.Avoid: Save your open files first: shutting down closes everything.
Guide.Hibernation.What: Puts a program "to sleep": it no longer opens or runs, but stays installed and can be woken up later.
Guide.Hibernation.Gain: Test whether you miss a program before uninstalling it for good.
Guide.Hibernation.When: When you're unsure whether you can remove a program.
Guide.Hibernation.Avoid: Don't put security programs or drivers to sleep.
Guide.StoreStartup.What: Lists the Microsoft Store apps that start on their own with Windows.
Guide.StoreStartup.Gain: Turn off Store apps that start with the PC without you asking.
Guide.StoreStartup.When: When apps like Teams, Spotify or Xbox open by themselves at startup.
Guide.StoreStartup.Avoid: For regular programs (outside the Store), use the Autorun Manager.
Guide.MsiDependencies.What: Shows which Windows Installer (MSI) packages depend on others.
Guide.MsiDependencies.Gain: Avoid removing a component another program needs.
Guide.MsiDependencies.When: Before removing components such as Visual C++ or .NET.
Guide.MsiDependencies.Avoid: If you only want to remove a regular program, you don't need to look here.
Guide.AppxCatalog.What: Lists every app package (Appx/MSIX) on Windows, including the factory-installed ones.
Guide.AppxCatalog.Gain: See what Windows and the Store installed, and where each package came from.
Guide.AppxCatalog.When: When you want to know everything that came with Windows.
Guide.AppxCatalog.Avoid: Many packages belong to the system and can't or shouldn't be removed.
Guide.SystemDlls.What: Lists libraries (DLLs) that programs left in the Windows system folders.
Guide.SystemDlls.Gain: Find files that old programs scattered across the system.
Guide.SystemDlls.When: For advanced users who want to clean leftovers in System32.
Guide.SystemDlls.Avoid: Deleting the wrong DLL can stop Windows or other programs from opening. When in doubt, leave it.
Guide.TrayIcon.What: Configures the Tranal icon next to the Windows clock.
Guide.TrayIcon.Gain: Keep Tranal at hand in the tray and hide it during uninstalls.
Guide.TrayIcon.When: If you use Tranal often and want to open it with one click.
Guide.TrayIcon.Avoid: If you don't use the tray, leave it as is.
Guide.NewInstalls.Gain: Find what got onto the PC without you noticing (programs bundled with other installers).
Guide.NewInstalls.When: After installing something and noticing extra programs or toolbars.
Guide.NewInstalls.Avoid: A new program isn't necessarily bad: check before removing.
Guide.ProgramCategories.What: Automatically groups programs by type (games, browsers, office, drivers…).
Guide.ProgramCategories.Gain: Find what you have installed more easily.
Guide.ProgramCategories.When: When the list is long and you want to see everything of one kind.
Guide.ProgramCategories.Avoid: The category is a guess from the name and publisher; there may be mistakes.
Guide.WindowsIntegration.What: Shows how Tranal appears in Windows (context menu, Control Panel) and shortcuts to the system tools.
Guide.WindowsIntegration.Gain: Turn "Uninstall with Tranal" in the Explorer right-click menu on or off.
Guide.WindowsIntegration.When: When you want to uninstall by right-clicking a shortcut.
Guide.WindowsIntegration.Avoid: If you don't use these shortcuts, there is no need to change anything.
Guide.Notifications.What: Shows the alerts and tips Tranal generated.
Guide.Notifications.When: When you want to read a Tranal message again.
Guide.Notifications.Avoid: It is not needed to use the program.
Guide.OperationProfiles.What: Sets default options per kind of operation (uninstall, clean…), such as creating a restore point or checking all leftovers.
Guide.OperationProfiles.Gain: No need to adjust the same options every time.
Guide.OperationProfiles.When: For people who uninstall many programs and always use the same options.
Guide.OperationProfiles.Avoid: The defaults are already safe; only change them if you know what each option does.
Guide.JunkCleaner.What: Looks for temporary files, caches, logs and thumbnails that Windows and programs pile up.
Guide.JunkCleaner.Gain: Free disk space without touching your documents.
Guide.JunkCleaner.When: When the disk is getting full, or every now and then.
Guide.JunkCleaner.Avoid: Close programs before cleaning. If a program keeps something important in its cache (drafts, for example), check the list before deleting.
Guide.WindowsTools.What: Shortcuts to Windows' own tools: disk cleanup, services, device manager, system restore and others.
Guide.WindowsTools.Gain: Reach the system tools quickly without digging through the Control Panel.
Guide.WindowsTools.When: When you know which Windows tool you want to open.
Guide.WindowsTools.Avoid: The tools open outside Tranal; use them with the usual care.
Guide.EvidenceRemover.What: Erases usage traces: recent documents, Explorer history, prefetch, event logs and DNS cache.
Guide.EvidenceRemover.Gain: More privacy: it gets harder to know what was opened on the computer.
Guide.EvidenceRemover.When: Before lending or selling the PC, or if it is shared.
Guide.EvidenceRemover.Avoid: You lose the "recent" lists and some convenience shortcuts. Event logs can help diagnose problems.
Guide.UnrecoverableDelete.What: Deletes files by overwriting their content first, so no recovery program can bring them back.
Guide.UnrecoverableDelete.Gain: Confidence that a sensitive file is truly gone.
Guide.UnrecoverableDelete.When: For sensitive documents (contracts, personal data) before selling or discarding the PC.
Guide.UnrecoverableDelete.Avoid: There is no going back: neither the Recycle Bin nor Tranal can recover it. Double-check what you picked.
Guide.HistoryCleaner.What: Clears Windows, browser and Office traces in one go.
Guide.HistoryCleaner.Gain: Privacy and a bit of free space, in one click.
Guide.HistoryCleaner.When: When you want to erase the history of everything at once.
Guide.HistoryCleaner.Avoid: You'll be signed out of websites and lose passwords stored only in cookies. To choose just one part, use the separate cleaners.
Guide.TracksBrowsers.What: Clears browser history, cookies, cache, form data and sessions.
Guide.TracksBrowsers.When: When the browser is slow or the computer is shared.
Guide.TracksBrowsers.Avoid: You'll be signed out of websites and lose the tabs of the previous session. Close the browser first.
Guide.TracksOffice.What: Clears the Microsoft Office recent documents list.
Guide.TracksOffice.Avoid: You lose the quick shortcut to recent documents in Office.
Guide.TracksWindows.What: Clears Windows traces: clipboard, recent items, search, thumbnails, temporary files and the Recycle Bin.
Guide.TracksWindows.When: Before handing the computer to someone else.
Guide.TracksWindows.Avoid: Whatever is in the Recycle Bin will be deleted for good.
Guide.RegistryOptimizer.What: Finds old Start menu and registry entries that point to programs that no longer exist.
Guide.RegistryOptimizer.Gain: A Start menu and Windows lists without broken items.
Guide.RegistryOptimizer.Avoid: The speed gain is small; the main benefit is tidiness.
Guide.RegistryCleaner.What: Looks for leftovers in the Windows registry from removed programs, grouped by category.
Guide.RegistryCleaner.Gain: A registry without broken references to programs that are gone.
Guide.RegistryCleaner.When: After uninstalls that left traces, or when a removed program still "shows up" somewhere.
Guide.RegistryCleaner.Avoid: Only remove what you're sure about. Tranal backs up first, but touching the registry without need doesn't make the PC faster.
Guide.PrivacyTraces.What: Shows what Windows keeps about how the computer is used (programs opened, recent files, searches).
Guide.PrivacyTraces.Gain: See and erase what reveals your usage habits.
Guide.PrivacyTraces.Avoid: Some traces power convenience features (recents, suggestions) that will stop working.
Guide.AlternateDataStreams.What: Finds content hidden "inside" files (NTFS alternate data streams) that Explorer doesn't show.
Guide.AlternateDataStreams.Gain: Discover hidden data that may be traces or something suspicious.
Guide.AlternateDataStreams.When: For security investigations or advanced cleanup.
Guide.AlternateDataStreams.Avoid: Windows uses these streams to mark files downloaded from the internet; deleting them removes that safety warning.
Guide.Unlocker.What: Shows who is holding a file or folder and releases the lock.
Guide.Unlocker.Gain: Delete or move files that Windows says are in use.
Guide.Unlocker.When: When you see "the file is open in another program".
Guide.Unlocker.Avoid: Forcing a file loose can make the program using it lose unsaved work.
Guide.InternetCleaner.What: Clears browser cookies, history, cache and forms, browser by browser.
Guide.InternetCleaner.Gain: Privacy and space, with control over what goes.
Guide.InternetCleaner.When: When you want to clean one specific browser.
Guide.InternetCleaner.Avoid: You'll be signed out of websites. Close the browser first.
Guide.DriveCleaner.What: Looks for unneeded files on the disk, grouped by category (logs, old backups, temporary files).
Guide.DriveCleaner.Gain: More free space with control over what is deleted.
Guide.DriveCleaner.When: When the disk is full and the temporary files cleanup wasn't enough.
Guide.DriveCleaner.Avoid: Check the list: .bak or .old files may be copies you want to keep.
Guide.ShortcutFixer.What: Finds Start menu and desktop shortcuts that point to programs that no longer exist.
Guide.ShortcutFixer.Gain: A Start menu and desktop without broken shortcuts.
Guide.ShortcutFixer.When: After uninstalling programs or changing disks.
Guide.ShortcutFixer.Avoid: Shortcuts to disconnected external drives show as broken; connect the drive first.
Guide.MruCleaner.What: Clears the "recently used" lists Windows keeps (Run, Open and Save boxes…).
Guide.MruCleaner.Gain: Privacy: hides what was typed and opened.
Guide.MruCleaner.Avoid: Open/save dialogs stop suggesting recent folders.
Guide.SharedDlls.What: Lists components shared between programs and how many programs use each one.
Guide.SharedDlls.Gain: Find components left orphaned after uninstalls.
Guide.SharedDlls.When: For advanced cleanup after many removals.
Guide.SharedDlls.Avoid: A shared component still in use must not be deleted. When in doubt, leave it.
Guide.RecycleBin.What: Shows what is in the Recycle Bin and lets you restore it or delete it for good.
Guide.RecycleBin.Gain: Recover something deleted by mistake, including leftovers removed by Tranal.
Guide.RecycleBin.When: When you miss a file after a cleanup.
Guide.RecycleBin.Avoid: Emptying the Recycle Bin deletes for good.
Guide.Finder.What: Searches files, folders and registry keys by name.
Guide.Finder.Gain: Find every remnant of a program scattered across the PC.
Guide.Finder.When: When you want to find leftovers of a program that was already removed.
Guide.Finder.Avoid: Results with generic names may belong to other programs; check before deleting.
Guide.RunOnce.What: Lists the actions Windows will run only once at the next sign-in.
Guide.RunOnce.Gain: See and cancel pending tasks that installers left behind.
Guide.RunOnce.When: When something odd happens every time you sign in to Windows.
Guide.RunOnce.Avoid: Some actions belong to updates in progress; cancel only what you recognize.
Guide.PendingOperations.What: Shows the files Windows will delete or rename at the next restart (including the ones Tranal postponed because they were in use).
Guide.PendingOperations.Gain: Know what is left to finish and why Windows asks for a restart.
Guide.PendingOperations.When: After an uninstall that asked for a restart.
Guide.PendingOperations.Avoid: Usually restarting the computer is enough; this is for special cases.
Guide.DailyRegistryBackup.What: Makes a copy of the Windows registry once a day, automatically, and lists the copies.
Guide.DailyRegistryBackup.Gain: A safety net: the registry can go back to an earlier day.
Guide.DailyRegistryBackup.When: If something went wrong after registry changes.
Guide.DailyRegistryBackup.Avoid: Restoring the registry undoes every change made after that day, including the good ones.
Guide.HexViewer.What: Shows the raw content of any file in hexadecimal and computes its checksum (hash).
Guide.HexViewer.Gain: Check whether a file is intact or investigate what it contains.
Guide.HexViewer.When: For technical users and checking downloads.
Guide.HexViewer.Avoid: Not needed if you only want to uninstall programs.
Guide.Bloatware.What: Lists programs that came with Windows or the computer and almost nobody uses.
Guide.Bloatware.Gain: A cleaner, lighter PC without programs you never asked for.
Guide.Bloatware.When: Right after buying the PC or reinstalling Windows.
Guide.Bloatware.Avoid: Some factory programs control special keys, battery or drivers. Look them up before removing ones from makers like Dell, HP or Lenovo.
Guide.Duplicates.What: Finds the same program installed twice (different versions or folders).
Guide.Duplicates.Gain: Free space and avoid conflicts between versions.
Guide.Duplicates.When: When a program appears twice in the list.
Guide.Duplicates.Avoid: Some programs need several versions installed on purpose (like Visual C++ or Java). Don't remove those.
Guide.Printers.What: Lists installed printers and the print queue.
Guide.Printers.Gain: Remove old printers and unstick jammed print jobs.
Guide.Printers.When: When a print job got stuck or there are printers you no longer use.
Guide.Printers.Avoid: Don't remove the printer you use every day.
Guide.CrashDumps.What: Finds the dump files Windows writes when a program or the system crashes.
Guide.CrashDumps.Gain: Free space — these files can be large.
Guide.CrashDumps.When: When the disk is full and there are no crashes to investigate.
Guide.CrashDumps.Avoid: If a technician is investigating crashes, they may need these files.
Guide.BrowserCleanup.What: Finds orphaned extensions and lets you reset the browser to its defaults.
Guide.BrowserCleanup.Gain: Fix a browser hijacked by ads or with a changed home page.
Guide.BrowserCleanup.When: When the browser changed its behavior on its own.
Guide.BrowserCleanup.Avoid: Resetting to defaults turns off extensions and may erase custom settings.
Guide.SoftwareUpdates.What: Checks whether there are new versions of the installed programs.
Guide.SoftwareUpdates.When: Every now and then, to keep the PC current.
Guide.SoftwareUpdates.Avoid: Some programs have their own updater; you can ignore them here.
Guide.AppUpdate.What: Checks for and installs new versions of Tranal itself.
Guide.AppUpdate.When: If automatic updates are turned off.
Guide.AppUpdate.Avoid: By default Tranal already updates itself.
Guide.UninstallHistory.What: Lists what you've already uninstalled, when, and what went with it, with the option to restore.
Guide.UninstallHistory.Gain: See what left the PC and undo a removal.
Guide.UninstallHistory.When: When you miss something you removed.
Guide.UninstallHistory.Avoid: Only uninstalls done by Tranal appear here.
Guide.CustomTools.What: Lets you register your own commands and programs to open from inside Tranal.
Guide.CustomTools.Gain: Keep the utilities you always use at hand.
Guide.CustomTools.When: For people who have favorite scripts or tools.
Guide.CustomTools.Avoid: Commands run with administrator rights; only register what you trust.
Guide.Processes.What: Shows what is running right now, which program it belongs to and how much it uses.
Guide.Processes.Gain: Find the program that slows the PC down and end it.
Guide.Processes.When: When the computer is freezing or the fan won't stop.
Guide.Processes.Avoid: Don't end Windows or antivirus processes.
Guide.SystemManagement.What: Brings together services, scheduled tasks, drivers and what each program leaves running in Windows.
Guide.SystemManagement.Gain: See everything a program spread across the system in one place.
Guide.SystemManagement.When: To clean services and tasks left over from removed programs.
Guide.SystemManagement.Avoid: Windows services and drivers are protected; other makers' ones may be needed for the hardware to work.
Guide.ContextMenu.What: Lists the Explorer right-click menu items from Tranal and other programs.
Guide.ContextMenu.Gain: A shorter, faster right-click menu without items from programs you don't use.
Guide.ContextMenu.When: When the right-click menu is huge or slow to open.
Guide.ContextMenu.Avoid: Hide instead of removing when in doubt.
Guide.Appearance.What: Shows programs on a size map, with a color legend and star ratings.
Guide.Appearance.Gain: See at a glance what takes up the most space.
Guide.Appearance.When: When you want to find the largest installed programs.
Guide.Appearance.Avoid: It's only a view; nothing is removed here.
Guide.SystemInfo.What: Shows computer information: Windows, processor, memory, disk, graphics and uptime.
Guide.SystemInfo.Gain: Have the PC details at hand for support or buying parts.
Guide.SystemInfo.When: When someone asks for your computer's specs.
Guide.SystemInfo.Avoid: It doesn't change anything on the system.
Guide.ProgramImpact.What: Shows which programs use the most processor and memory.
Guide.ProgramImpact.Gain: Find out what slows the computer down.
Guide.ProgramImpact.When: When the PC is slow and you want to know the culprit.
Guide.ProgramImpact.Avoid: A program being heavy while you use it (like a game) is normal; look at what weighs when you're not using it.
Guide.CrashAnalyzer.What: Groups the failures recorded by Windows by program.
Guide.CrashAnalyzer.When: When programs close by themselves or the PC restarts out of nowhere.
Guide.CrashAnalyzer.Avoid: It doesn't fix the failure; it helps you decide whether to update or remove the program.
Guide.Relocation.What: Lists programs moved from one disk to another and lets you move them back.
Guide.Relocation.Gain: Undo a disk move that caused trouble.
Guide.Relocation.When: If a moved program stopped opening.
Guide.Relocation.Avoid: If you never moved programs, the list is empty.
Nav.ForcedTip: For programs that are not in the list or whose uninstaller is broken: point to the file or folder and Tranal removes what it finds.
Page.Programs.Subtitle: Pick a program and click Uninstall. Tranal runs the program's own uninstaller and then finds and removes what it left behind.
Search.Placeholder: Search programs by name or publisher
Action.UninstallTip: Opens the wizard: confirms with you, creates a restore point, runs the program's uninstaller and looks for leftovers.
Action.QuickUninstallTip: Uninstalls with the recommended options, without the review screens. Only high-confidence leftovers are removed.
Selection.None.Title: No program selected
Selection.None.Hint: Click a program in the list. Double-click to uninstall right away.
Selection.Many.Title: {0} programs selected
Selection.Many.Hint: They will be uninstalled one at a time.
Tools.Title: Tools
Tools.Subtitle: Extra features to clean, speed up and take care of Windows. None of them is needed to uninstall programs — open only what makes sense for you. Each tool explains what it does before you use it.
Options.HardwareRendering: Use the graphics card to draw the window (uses more memory)
